slides.title: Does Wudu wash only your body?
slides.promise: My Prayer follows the water from limb to limb and asks what each one has been doing.

slides.head: Where the water has to show
slides.body: The meaning of water is incomplete within us if nothing of it appears in our dealings.

slides.head: A visible mercy
slides.body: My Prayer calls water a visible mercy. Each limb is a pause for reflection, so the water passes over the heart as over the body.

slides.head: The hands
slides.body: The hands were created to work, build and give. As the water reaches them, ask what they have been doing.

slides.head: The mouth
slides.body: A mouth that will read al-Fatihah shouldn't willingly backbite, lie or wound.

slides.head: The face and the arms
slides.body: A face that prostrates to its Lord shouldn't rise in arrogance over His servants. The arms should support truth rather than oppression.

slides.head: The head and the feet
slides.body: The head bows in worship to none but Allah. At the feet, the book asks about the roads they walk.

slides.quote: Where am I going, and does this road bring me closer to the destination for which I ask in al-Fatihah?

slides.head: Wudu gathers the whole person
items: Hands: made to work, build and give.
Mouth: never willingly backbite, lie or wound.
Face and arms: humble, and on the side of truth.
Head: bowed to none but Allah.
Feet: on a road that brings you closer.

slides.head: Read more in My Prayer
